metric.note: Kernel geomeans are over each mode's correct stems. The composition and sequential deltas are paired: both halves are scored over the stems that are clean on both sides, so they share a denominator.

drkernel.name: Dr. Kernel
drkernel.loop: 8 samples x 3 generate-execute-feedback turns per operator

claude.name: Claude Code
claude.loop: One session per operator with the default tools (5 h cap)

kda.name: KDA
kda.loop: One planning cycle, then two implement-review rounds (6 h cap)

ako.name: AKO
ako.loop: Two master-directed sub-agent rewrite rounds (5 h cap per round)

codex.name: Codex
codex.loop: One session per operator, same prompt as Claude Code (5 h cap)

agents.description: Kernel-generation agents on FastKernels L1-L3 plus the end-to-end MacroEval of their winner sets.

models.description: Base models behind one fixed agent scaffold (vanilla-agents-fastkernels), so the only variable is the model. Ranked by correct-rate x geomean; see docs/leaderboard/MODEL_BOARD.md for the scope.

scope_note.question: Whether the model or the scaffold around it does the work. The agent board's Codex row is already one point on this axis -- it is gpt-5.6-sol under exactly this scaffold -- so the board would extend that point rather than open a new axis.
scope_note.why_deferred: The models reachable from this scaffold are three same-family GPT variants plus one Claude, all closed-weights, which is too narrow a spread to rank meaningfully. CommBench already ranks base models on GPU code across an open-weights spread.
scope_note.unblocked_by: An open-weights endpoint the scaffold can reach. The runner and scoring are in place and validated against the agent board, so adding models is a matter of machine time, not engineering.
